nodes.label: Linux capture provider input-density gate
nodes.summary: Same claim already emitted by chunk-rem-009, chunk-rem-100, chunk-rem-108 and chunk-rem-115. This note reaches it from the writer side rather than the capture-provider side: the worker guards on `if let Some(input) = sample.input_density`, so a Linux sample with `input_density: None` inserts no raw event at all, and every downstream reader that filters on `event_type == "input_density"` sees an empty timeline.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - inventory-prior-docs-and-known-issues [ses_f2592cfaeffe5WZOY3OHInhsF9].md:L6006] the only writer of the `input_density` raw event (`worker.rs:462`, `event_type: "input_density".to_string()`). With `None`, no row is ever inserted.

nodes.label: A frontend poll-cadence requirement is not a data fix
nodes.norm_label: frontend poll cadence requirement is not a data fix
nodes.summary: The desktop-tray-idle-memory plan gates Digital Tracker activity refresh on renderer visibility. That stops polling while the window is hidden and changes nothing about whether the data exists, so it is often mistaken for the fix for a blank tracker on Linux.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - inventory-prior-docs-and-known-issues [ses_f2592cfaeffe5WZOY3OHInhsF9].md:L6073] This is purely a **frontend poll-cadence** requirement (stop refreshing while the window is hidden). It is orthogonal to whether the underlying data exists. It is not a fix for the blank tracker and must not be cited as one.

nodes.label: Wayland backend plan is scoped to triggers, not activity capture
nodes.norm_label: wayland backend plan is scoped to triggers not activity capture
nodes.summary: The 2026-09-22 Wayland plan lands an evdev hook for typed-trigger detection and uinput injection. It never touches activity/capture_provider.rs or activity/hardware_events.rs, so the evdev capability it adds is not consumed by the Digital Tracker even though the plan reads as a Wayland fix.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - inventory-prior-docs-and-known-issues [ses_f2592cfaeffe5WZOY3OHInhsF9].md:L6067] The plan is scoped to *trigger detection* (`keyboard/evdev_hook.rs`) and *injection*. It never touches `activity/capture_provider.rs` or `activity/hardware_events.rs`. Anyone reading the Wayland plan alone could reasonably conclude the tracker was fixed on Wayland. It was not.

nodes.label: The accepted-degradation baseline is narrower than the observed behaviour
nodes.norm_label: accepted degradation baseline is narrower than the observed behaviour
nodes.summary: linux-setup.md is the only accepted-degradation baseline in the repo, and it conditions the blank tracker on a missing xorg-xprop/kdotool helper while separately admitting there are no input-density counts on Linux. The three downstream metrics derive solely from those counts, so the baseline does not cover the symptom it is cited against.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-25 - inventory-prior-docs-and-known-issues [ses_f2592cfaeffe5WZOY3OHInhsF9].md:L6135] **The "by design" claim is narrower than the actual behavior.** The doc says the tracker goes blank *only* when a helper is missing ("Without `xorg-xprop`/`kdotool` samples come back empty and the tracker stays blank"). It separately admits "no input-density counts" unconditionally on Linux — but the downstream metrics (`analytics_events.quantity`, `duration_ms`, `focus_duration_ms`) are computed *solely* from those missing counts. So even with both helpers installed, input events / tracked duration / focused duration remain zero. **The doc's "by design" framing does not actually cover the observed symptom**, which means your RCA is not contradicting an accepted decision; it is filling a documentation gap the decision never covered.

nodes.label: A bare YYYY-MM-DD string parses as UTC midnight, not local midnight
nodes.norm_label: bare date string parses as utc midnight not local midnight
nodes.summary: `new Date("2026-01-15")` is UTC midnight by specification, which is the previous local day anywhere west of Greenwich. Seven call sites compared that instant against a local-midnight anchor, so every one of them was off by a day. Replaced with parseLocalDate.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - f3b-extend-local-date-parse [ses_f2096ccbdffeognW39r8Hfzq6E].md:L1878] `new Date("2026-01-15")` → UTC midnight. In New York, that's 2026-01-14 19:00 local. `dueStart` = local midnight of Jan 14. `todayStart` = local midnight of today. So diffDays is one less than intended. So a task due 2026-01-15 with today = 2026-01-15 would compute dueStart = Jan 14 midnight, todayStart = Jan 15 midnight → diffDays = -1 → "Overdue". **That's a real bug: due today reads Overdue.**

nodes.label: A uniform date shift preserves relative order but corrupts bucket boundaries
nodes.norm_label: uniform date shift preserves order but corrupts bucket boundaries
nodes.summary: taskSort applied the same one-day shift to every date, so within-bucket ordering by aTime is preserved and a pure-bare-date sort really does emit the same order. The Today/Tomorrow versus overdue grouping is still wrong, which is why a passing order-only probe case does not clear the site.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - f3b-extend-local-date-parse [ses_f2096ccbdffeognW39r8Hfzq6E].md:L1892] **So the claim "ordering is unaffected" is only true for relative order among dated tasks — but the bucket assignment IS affected.** The sibling's claim that "ordering is unaffected" is partially wrong

nodes.label: Module-scope env assignment must precede a static import
nodes.norm_label: module scope env must be set before a static import
nodes.summary: The probe pinned TZ at module scope and pulled the modules under test in with a top-level `await import()`. A static import would have hoisted above the assignment, so the timezone would have been read after the modules initialised and the probe would have passed for the wrong reason.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - f3b-extend-local-date-parse [ses_f2096ccbdffeognW39r8Hfzq6E].md:L6729] `process.env.TZ` is set at **module scope** and the modules under test are pulled in with top-level `await import()` (a static `import` would hoist above it — the exact mistake that makes this probe class lie).

nodes.label: A mid-day probe proves nothing for a clock-dependent flip
nodes.norm_label: mid day probe proves nothing for a clock dependent flip
nodes.summary: The sortMagicMenuTasks misparse only changes the tier in the last few hours of the local day, because the bare date is compared against a real instant. Probed at 13:00 the before and after tiers are identical, so an early attempt at the case was a false positive and the clock had to move to 22:00.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - f3b-extend-local-date-parse [ses_f2096ccbdffeognW39r8Hfzq6E].md:L6766] The flip only happens in the *last `offset` hours* of the local day (20:00–24:00 in EDT): a task due **tomorrow** read as overdue and, on the priority tiebreak, outranked a genuinely overdue task. At 13:00 the tier is identical before and after, so a mid-day probe proves nothing — my first attempt at this case was a false positive and I moved the clock to 22:00.

nodes.label: A Tauri invoke of a Result<T,E> where T is a plain struct never resolves null
nodes.norm_label: tauri invoke of a result never resolves null
nodes.summary: list_rollback_versions returns Result<RollbackVersions, String> and RollbackVersions is a plain struct of three non-Option fields, registered once. Tauri resolves Ok(T) and rejects Err(E), so the only producer of the null that crashed the hook was a test mock falling through to `return null`.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - fix-pre-existing-typeerror-in-backup-state [ses_f174462a1ffeZq6ybDWaqKo6Zo].md:L3381] Tauri maps `Ok(T)` → resolve `T`, `Err(E)` → reject. So the promise resolves a populated object or rejects. It **cannot** resolve `null`.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - fix-pre-existing-typeerror-in-backup-state [ses_f174462a1ffeZq6ybDWaqKo6Zo].md:L3382] `RollbackVersions` is a plain struct with three non-`Option` fields (`String, String, Vec<_>`). Serde serializes it to an object, never `null`.

nodes.label: A hook's own catch swallows a deref and writes it to the user-visible error slot
nodes.norm_label: hooks own catch swallows a deref into the user visible error slot
nodes.summary: The payload.versions deref threw inside the function's own try, so the same function's catch caught it and assigned the raw TypeError text into rollbackError, which ApplicationUpdatesSection renders whenever the string does not match the friendly-error regex. The internal JS error reached the user instead of the suite failing.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - fix-pre-existing-typeerror-in-backup-state [ses_f174462a1ffeZq6ybDWaqKo6Zo].md:L3385] it was thrown *inside* the function's own `try`, so the function's own `catch` swallowed it and wrote the raw text into `rollbackError` — the user-visible error slot. `ApplicationUpdatesSection.tsx:212-214` renders that string to the user when it does not match the friendly-error regex.

nodes.label: An adjacent null-coalesce shows the payload was already treated as partial
nodes.norm_label: adjacent null coalesce shows the payload was already treated as partial
nodes.summary: The same function already wrote `payload.current ?? null` on the next line, and a test already returns current: null even though the type declares current: string. The file had adopted a partial-payload standard and left only versions — the one field dereferenced and assigned into array state — bare, which is the stated reason the guard is warranted rather than speculative.

The author already treated this payload as possibly-partial; only `versions` — the one field dereferenced and assigned into array state — was left bare.

nodes.label: A realistic mock revives a previously-dead code path
nodes.norm_label: realistic mock revives a previously dead code path
nodes.summary: Under the old null payload, loadRollbackVersions returned null from its catch, so persistRollbackSkip(null, null) hit the `if (!rolledFrom) return` guard and set_preference update_ignore_version was never invoked. The existing assertion still passed, so the test had been green for the wrong reason; fixing the mock turned the dead path live without weakening an assertion.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - fix-pre-existing-typeerror-in-backup-state [ses_f174462a1ffeZq6ybDWaqKo6Zo].md:L3417] the mock fix made a **previously-dead code path live**. Under the old `null`, `loadRollbackVersions` returned `null` from its catch, so `persistRollbackSkip(null, null)` hit the `if (!rolledFrom) return` guard and `set_preference update_ignore_version` was **never** invoked — that test was passing for the wrong reason. It now runs the real path. No assertion was weakened or added.
